Let's remind ourselves of the special trigonometric ratios, as given by the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/dbf36192ac332dc49ed75278838e989a37ac7d888311be1b8b059a7b59667aa6.png)

From the unit circle, we see that the angle $\frac{\pi }{3}$ corresponds to the point $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}).$

- Since the cosine of the angle corresponds to the $x$-coordinate, we have $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{1}{2}.$

- Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the $y$-coordinate, we have $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$

Therefore, using the fact that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$
